close_reason:
Applied option B from the bead: dropped struct-level #[serde(default)] from ChatCapability and ChatPushCapability while keeping #[derive(Default)] for test ergonomics. Field-level #[serde(default)] on supported_body_types preserved per its own rustdoc rationale. max_messages_per_push stays Option<u64> (already-optional spec field per chat-push-00 line 96).

5 regression tests added pinning the new strict behavior:
- ChatCapability {} -> Err
- ChatCapability missing maxBodyBytes -> Err
- ChatPushCapability {} -> Err
- ChatPushCapability missing supportedUrgencyValues -> Err
- ChatPushCapability with both required fields + no maxMessagesPerPush -> Ok (optional field still optional)

Existing tests all pass — none relied on the silent-zero behavior. Struct rustdoc on both types now documents the strictness decision and cites the spec lines (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §3 lines 171-184 and draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00 lines 90-94).

cargo test -p jmap-chat-client: 52 lib tests pass (was 47, +5 new). cargo test --workspace green. cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean. cargo fmt clean. Committed as 2b99b06.
description: src/session.rs:22-25, 80-81. ChatCapability and ChatPushCapability both have BOTH #[derive(..., Default)] AND struct-level #[serde(default)]. Wire object `{}` deserializes successfully with max_body_bytes=0, max_attachment_bytes=0, etc. — all spec-mandated fields silently zero. draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §3 lines 171-184 mark these as required (not optional). A server returning {} is non-compliant; a client treating max_body_bytes=0 as real will refuse to send any message. Worse: the bug is silent. Fix (option B from review): drop the struct-level #[serde(default)] but keep Default derive for test ergonomics. Keep field-level #[serde(default)] on supported_body_types (its rustdoc on lines 46-50 justifies that one as forward-compat). Same fix applies to ChatPushCapability — maxSnippetBytes and supportedUrgencyValues are spec-required (chat-push-00 lines 90-94); only maxMessagesPerPush is optional (line 96, already Option<u64>). AGENTS.md 'Default impls that hardcode values the spec does not mandate' is the exact antipattern.
title: ChatCapability struct-level #[serde(default)] masks non-compliant servers
